profile_text.body:
The Allen Institute for AI (also known as Ai2) is a nonprofit research laboratory founded in 2014 by Paul Allen and headquartered in Seattle, WA. Led by Ali Farhadi, the organization describes itself as conducting high-impact research and engineering to tackle key problems in artificial intelligence, guided by open, collaborative, and inclusive principles aimed at producing safe, ethical, and trustworthy AI systems. The institute works with external partners including the University of Washington's Paul G. Allen School of Computer Science and Engineering, the NSF on an open multimodal AI infrastructure project intended to accelerate scientific discovery, and Google Cloud on the development of open AI models and platforms for environmental and scientific research.

Ai2's AI work spans foundational language modeling and applied scientific domains. Its open-source language model, OLMo, is developed with fully open training data and an emphasis on research transparency, consistent with the organization's nonprofit mission. Semantic Scholar is the institute's academic search tool, offering paper summaries and citation graphs to support the research community. The site also highlights applications of AI to climate science, agriculture and food security, wildfire management, and wildlife and ecosystem protection.
